jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Before Photo
jokes.joke: I hired a personal trainer because I wanted a dramatic before-and-after photo. Six months later, he took another picture and said, “Wow, you’ve really transformed.” I said, “Where?” He said, “Your posture.” So now I’m still fat, but I’m presenting it with confidence.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Spot Me
jokes.joke: I hired a personal trainer to help me hit my goal weight. Six months later, he hit his goal weight. I paid for his cruise. He said I 'built incredible character.' I said, 'I wanted a six-pack, not a personality.' Now he texts me motivational quotes from the boat. I'm not even mad, I'm just still fat and somehow also funding his tan.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: A Little off the Top
jokes.joke: Never walk into a hair salon and tell the stylist, 'I'm feeling spontaneous, just do whatever you want.' To me, 'spontaneous' means cutting off an extra half-inch. To a twenty-two-year-old stylist named Jax, 'spontaneous' means giving a grown man a bleached asymmetrical mullet. I didn't leave looking fresh and edgy. I left looking like I owe back child support in 1996.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Deadpan Deadlifts
jokes.joke: I hired a personal trainer who's completely humorless. During lunges last week I cracked, 'If the weights don't kill me, the silence will.' He just adjusted my form and said, 'Core.' Now I pay eighty bucks an hour to suffer next to a guy who treats every joke like a surprise tax audit.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Trainer Trouble
jokes.joke: I hired a personal trainer to help me finally get in shape, and after three months he sat me down and said, “Look, man… I think your real fitness goal is just showing up late and leaving early.” I told him, “Exactly. And I’m proud to say I’ve hit that target every single day.”

scores.comment: Clear premise and several usable tags, but the cruise/character escalation is somewhat predictable and the final tan line is weaker than the six-pack/personality line.
Strong concrete setup, natural escalation, vivid haircut image, and a genuinely punchy final comparison. The 1996 child-support turn is unexpected and carries the laugh.
Clean and understandable, but the humorless-trainer premise follows an obvious route and the tax-audit comparison feels familiar rather than distinctive.
Competent self-deprecating bit with clean timing, but the reversal is easy to anticipate and the final line mostly confirms the setup rather than sharply heightening it.
Clean turn on 'posture,' solid closer, but the reframe-as-victory shape is familiar.
Specific character work (Jax) and a vivid, unexpected closing image; best escalation of the batch.
‘Surprise tax audit’ simile lands well; solid but slightly familiar humorless-trainer premise.
Punchline mostly restates the setup’s reframing joke; competent but predictable and low surprise.
Good rhythm and clean phrasing, but the 'posture over weight loss' pivot feels slightly familiar.
Excellent reversal. The premise of inadvertently funding the trainer's success is fresh, and 'wanted a six-pack, not a personality' is a strong, natural stage line.
Solidly constructed deadpan dynamic. The pacing works well, and the closing tax audit simile provides a respectable payoff.
Competent filler. Reframing the failure to work out as hitting a target of laziness is a very standard, predictable comic shape.
Clean posture twist and confident-fat closer; solid but familiar gym-fail shape.
Strong premise that the trainer succeeds; cruise and tan tags add bite though slightly overpacked.
Clear warning setup, specific stylist mismatch, and sharp 1996 child-support closer land cleanly.
Simple inversion of goals into showing up late; competent but thin payoff.
Clean premise and a confident final image; solid but not sharply surprising.
Fun escalation with the trainer’s cruise; the closer lands mildly but clearly.
Strong premise, vivid imagery, and a memorable final line; genuinely good joke.
Clear setup and a tidy closer; relatable, though not especially surprising.
